entityName: Hamburg University of Technology - Smart Sensors Group
entityDescription:
The Smart Sensors Group at the Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) specializes in the development of resource-efficient digital systems for use under extreme conditions. The Smart Sensors Group’s general research focuses on digital data and signal processing on smart sensors, real-time data processing, energy-efficient processing, as well as reliability, fault tolerance, and embedded fault diagnosis, with numerous previous projects demonstrating expertise in these areas (PotatoNet, REAP, INGA, 5GSatOpt, TRIPLE-nanoAUV/TRIPLE-MoDo). Furthermore, the group has more than 10 years of experience in research on the energy efficiency of embedded systems, enabling energy-autonomous operation of sensor systems through low-power processing strategies in both hardware and software.
A key application focus of the Smart Sensors Group’s research lies in the field of sensors under space conditions as well as space electronics, where extremely high reliability is required. In the ongoing space projects AuRelia and SArES, funded by the DLR and BMFTR, methods for the autonomous yet reliable operation of an SCG sensor under space conditions are currently being researched and developed, complemented by the SatelLight project for intra-satellite communication using LiFi. As part of the EduSat project, a CubeSat is currently being developed in collaboration with students as part of a teaching and research initiative.
The Smart Sensors Group is currently involved in numerous IOV missions, including the MAPHEUS-15 campaign and the development of a payload for the DLR satellites PLUTO I and PLUTO II.

TUHH: The Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) is a public university in Hamburg and is one of the youngest technical universities in Germany. It was founded in 1978.
Approximately 100 professors teach the 7,400 students in 35 bachelor’s and master’s degree programs. A distinctive feature of the university is its organization into research fields and academic deans’ offices instead of traditional faculties, which enables closer collaboration among the various institutes. There are six academic deans’ offices (Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Mathematics, Management Sciences and Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Technology and Innovation in Education, and Process Engineering) as well as the interdisciplinary field of Engineering Sciences and Technologies.

Euphyia Tech Ltd is a Cyprus-based technology company specialising in digital solutions for smarter, more sustainable and future-ready buildings. Established as a spin-off of Frederick University and Frederick Research Center, Euphyia develops cloud-based tools that support the assessment, benchmarking and improvement of building performance, with a focus on smart readiness, lifecycle sustainability, building intelligence and digital visualisation.
The company’s product ecosystem includes Smart Ready Go!, a platform for Smart Readiness Indicator assessment and improvement planning; EcoHestia, a lifecycle environmental assessment platform for buildings; and Smart BEAR, a smartness assessment and VR-based visualisation platform. Euphyia combines building physics, sustainability assessment, BIM/IFC integration, data analytics and software engineering to transform advanced research methodologies into practical, market-ready digital services.
For ESA-related activities, Euphyia is interested in developing space-enabled services that use Earth observation and satellite-derived data to support climate-neutral, smart and resilient buildings. Relevant areas include building renovation prioritisation, urban climate resilience mapping, cooling demand and summer energy poverty observatories, renewable energy and heat-pump suitability mapping, embodied carbon monitoring, and digital twins enriched with space-based environmental data.
Euphyia seeks collaboration with partners active in Earth observation, satellite data processing, urban analytics, climate services, municipalities, energy agencies and building-sector innovation.

entityDescription:
SYCONS Kft. was founded in 1990 by private persons, and is in 100% Hungarian ownership until this day. In the beginning, our activities consisted of trenchless utility construction, technical consulting for ground surface stabilization projects, and application of state-of-the-art trenchless (No-Dig) utility rehabilitation technologies mainly abroad (Kuwait, Libya).
Today our company is a key actor of the underground construction industry in Hungary. We offer complex solutions of utility construction, environment protection, specialized underground works, earthworks and road construction works to our Partners.
Thanks to the long years of experiences of our colleagues, we are able to offer services of the highest level to our clients. From the beginning, we continuously develop our know-how and equipment, and we continuously seek new, innovative underground construction solutions, based on old, well-proven technologies.
Our patented deep drilled drainage system construction technology offers a unique solution since March 2001 for the stabilization of loose, dangerous embankments or other ground surface movements.
One of our most important references is the construction of METRO line 4, where we performed protective layer stabilizations using one our new technologies, the soil anchoring, combined with an old technology (pipe jacking).
Our second patent has been developed in 2015: this is the construction technology of drainpipe installation by high-precision (in cm) directional drilling in great depth, in high lengths.
We are proud to be known by our partners as a company being able to offer technical solutions even when others considers the task insoluble.
 
Our objective:
- Complete execution of complex, big projects, in continuous contact with the client.
- Identification of the best technical/economical solution for underground construction tasks to be executed by investors, designers or municipalities, that often seem insoluble using traditional technologies.
- Participation in the solution of a given task or problem, even already in design phase. 
- Elaboration of complete solutions in collaboration with our partners, using our professional experiences.
- Flexible and economic execution of our projects in perfect quality.
Our company, as a company executing underground construction works, attaches importance to be member of different professional organizations, and to support them by our professional experiences and financial aids.
We participate in the activities of the following organizations: 
- HSTT - Hungarian Society for Trenchless Technologies
- Association of Hungarian Water Well Drillers
 
We are active participants of the following conference series, even as lecturers: 
- Geotechnical conferences
- Geological sources of danger - conferences
- NO-DIG conferences
 
Other organizations, of which our colleagues are members:
- Hungarian Chamber of Engineers
- Hungarian Society of Hydrology
Furthermore, we attach a particular importance to professionally and financially support the professional activities of the educational institutions.
In the last years, we supported the activities of the below listed institutions and organizations:
- Budapest University of Technology and Economics

ADENERA is a technology company based in Slovenia, specialising in the application of Earth Observation data and artificial intelligence to electricity grid operations. The company develops data-driven services that give electricity distribution operators and other energy-sector actors improved visibility of distributed generation and consumption patterns across their networks. Its core technology combines satellite observation, weather modelling, and machine learning to derive operational insight at network scale, without requiring additional on-site measurement infrastructure. The services are delivered digitally and are designed to integrate with the operational and planning systems already used by network operators.

ADENERA's team brings together competences in electricity grid operations, network planning, and energy market regulation, alongside AI and data engineering and the commercialisation of technology-based services. The company operates at the intersection of space-based data and energy infrastructure, addressing the growing need for scalable, non-intrusive solutions that support the management of rapidly expanding distributed renewable generation in Europe and beyond. The company was founded as a spin-off of Abelium d. o. o., a Slovenian data science and AI firm with established experience in system architecture, machine learning model development, and analytics for the energy sector, in order to commercialise services developed under the ESA ARTES 4.0 Downstream Applications programme.

ColliMate Space R&D S.L. is a space technology company developing AI-driven software to optimize satellite communications and data transport across space and ground networks. The company’s core platform enables autonomous, real-time orchestration of data flows, improving latency, reliability, and cost efficiency in increasingly congested and dynamic space environments. By combining physics-based models with machine learning, ColliMate Space enhances decision-making for satellite operators, ground station providers, and government users.
A key aspect of the platform is its capability to process and leverage signal intelligence (SIGINT) and RF data to improve situational awareness and optimize communication strategies. Its technology addresses critical bottlenecks in space data delivery, enabling faster access to time-sensitive information for applications such as Earth observation, defense, and emergency response.

In addition, the company develops capabilities aligned with Delay/Disruption Tolerant Networking (DTN) and next-generation communication protocols to enable resilient data transport across LEO, cislunar, and deep space environments. These capabilities support operations over heterogeneous and intermittently connected networks, enabling adaptive routing, scheduling, and resource allocation under dynamic link conditions, interference, and environmental constraints.

dataHEARD is a Geneva-based non-profit association dedicated to transforming fragmented health and environmental data into integrated, actionable systems. We work across four pillars: collaboration and advocacy, capacity building, innovation and technology, and research and monitoring services. Through technical assistance, south-to-south learning, and responsible use of digital innovation, we empower low- and middle-income countries to make evidence-based decisions that strengthen resilience, inform policy, and drive sustainable impact. Based at the heart of global decision-making in Geneva, we operate across borders to ensure that every relevant insight is counted and heard.
Our vision is simple: a future where every country and community owns its data and uses it to thrive.
